title: Joining the board of a Harlem cultural center
summary: He speaks up to the board that includes Belafonte and Davis about including present-day musicians.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: So the idea is that we must begin now, and say now, and I'm willing to be one of the creators...I've...incidentally, I've just been named as one of the members of the board of a cultural thing that we're doing here in central Harlem... they're going to spend seventy or eighty million dollars on this project and I'm on the Board of Directors. And I most certainly intend to see...and what actually happened was that Assemblyman George W. Miller called a meeting to report on this affair and the board members consisted of Harry Belafonte and Ossie Davis and great guys who've already made it. But I got up and I said to them, 'You have got to have some of the present day people who are here on the scene to have some input in this thing. Because you can't tell me that you can have a garage two blocks away from a center and not determine how the people are going to get from that garage to the center and from the center back to the garage. It's the same as with the subway, and whatever idea that you adopt can be...probably be the idea that you can use to create a better tone in central Harlem, or in Harlem, whereby that blacks can become more interested in jazz.'
